To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the IceCube data can be explained with neutrino decays and pseudo-Dirac-neutrinos; (ii) the Icecube data can be explained without the need for new physics, such as a sterile neutrino, or a new interaction; (iii) the IceCUBE data can be explained if neutrinos decay into a light sterile neutrino, with a lifetime τ _{ν}  = 10 ^{-3}  s.
neutrino decay and pseudo-Dirac neutrinos are able to explain the IceCube data, and that the IceCube data are consistent with a non-zero neutrino mass.

the question whether the IceCube results can be reconciled with the theoretical predictions of high-energy astroparticle physics.
the possible existence of exotic properties of neutrinos and their impact on astrophysical neutrino fluxes.
the possible explanation of the IceCube non-observation of high-energy muons in the PeV region.

the high-energy muon flux is low, and this is consistent with neutrino decay or pseudo-Dirac neutrinos.
the IceCube data do not exclude the possibility that the high-energy neutrino flux is suppressed due to exotic properties of neutrinos.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the neutrino fluxes are consistent with the IceCube results for the energy region below 100 PeV, but the neutrino flux is significantly suppressed at energies beyond 100 PeVs.
we show that the IceCube data are not inconsistent with the standard model of particle physics.
we have not been able to find any solution to the IceCube anomaly, but we have found that the neutrino decay solution would be a possible solution if there is a new physics beyond the Standard Model.

the high-energy neutrino flux is sensitive to the neutrino mass hierarchy, and to the possibility that neutrinos are pseudo-Dirac particles.
